focus_area: Frontend: template modals, automation modal, and job setup

findings.requirement: SubjectPreview styled component (also: spec known failure pattern #1)
findings.description: SubjectPreview uses `font-size: ${t.text.sm};` but `t.text.sm` is a complete CSS declaration that already includes the `font-size:` property. This produces invalid CSS like `font-size: font-size: 0.875rem;`. Every other file in the codebase uses `t.text.sm` standalone in a template literal array (e.g., `${[t.text.sm]}`), never inside a `font-size:` property. The spec assignment explicitly asked to check for this bug, and it is present. Fix: replace `font-size: ${t.text.sm};` with `${t.text.sm}` (standalone).

findings.requirement: Automation modal's existing-template preview should show subject
findings.description: The spec says 'Automation modal's existing-template preview: show the saved template's subject as-is.' The existing-template preview section (lines 401-406 in the source file) renders `selectedTemplate.body` via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` but does NOT render `selectedTemplate.subject`. The diff does not modify this section. When a user selects an existing template in the automation modal, they see the body preview but have no visibility into the template's subject. Fix: add subject display above the body preview in the existing-template preview section, similar to how ChannelMessageTemplateSelectionModal's PreviewSelection shows `mailMerge.subjectRaw`.

findings.requirement: Validation repopulation of subject with default on error
findings.description: The spec's validation strategy says 'On submit with a cleared field, fire the standard form-error AND repopulate the field with the rendered default so the user sees the baseline.' BulkMessageModal (diff lines 176-178) and ChannelMessageNew (diff lines 452-455) both repopulate subject with the default when validation fails with a blank subject. ChannelMessageTemplateModal does NOT — its handleSubmit else branch only calls `setErrors(validationErrors)` without repopulating the subject. A user who clears the subject field and submits will see the error but the field remains empty, requiring manual re-entry of the default. Fix: add `if (!subject || subject.trim() === '') { setChannelMessageTemplate(prev => ({...prev, subject: defaultSubject})); }` in the validation-failure branch.

The subject input's onChange handler is `handleChangeChannelMessageName`. While this handler works correctly because it uses the `[name]: value` dynamic key pattern and `name="subject"` is set on the input, the handler name is misleading — it was originally written for the template name field. Every other surface in the diff creates a dedicated handler for subject changes (e.g., `handleChangeSubject`, `handleChangeNewTemplateSubject`). This is a code clarity issue, not a functional bug.
